sections.content: You know *en mi opinión*, *aunque*, *además* and *en conclusión* from earlier units (B1 Unit 25 and B1 Unit 33). A sustained argument connects a position, supporting reasons, concessions and a conclusion, and uses these connectors to signal movement between ideas.

items.spanish: En mi opinión, la propuesta merece apoyo porque ofrece una solución práctica.
items.english: In my opinion, the proposal deserves support because it offers a practical solution.

items.spanish: Aunque tiene algunas limitaciones, sus ventajas son importantes para la comunidad.
items.english: Although it has some limitations, its advantages are important for the community.

items.spanish: Además, la evidencia disponible sugiere que podría funcionar a largo plazo.
items.english: Furthermore, the available evidence suggests that it could work in the long term.

items.spanish: En conclusión, considero que deberíamos aplicarla, siempre que se revisen sus resultados.
items.english: In conclusion, I consider that we should implement it, provided that its results are reviewed.

sections.content: New here: a condition can be built into your conclusion with *siempre que*, *con tal de que* ("provided that", "as long as") or *a menos que* ("unless"). All three take the present subjunctive: *Apoyo la medida siempre que sea justa.*

items.spanish: Podemos aplicar la propuesta siempre que tengamos los recursos.
items.english: We can implement the proposal as long as we have the resources.

items.spanish: Acepto el cambio con tal de que todos puedan participar.
items.english: I accept the change provided that everyone can take part.

items.spanish: No cambiaré de opinión a menos que haya más evidencia.
items.english: I will not change my mind unless there is more evidence.

sections.content: In a debate, acknowledge a reasonable opposing point before explaining why your own conclusion remains stronger.
